feature_overview.business_goal: Allow team members to discuss a task in context by adding comments, so work-related conversations stay attached to the task instead of scattered across email or chat.
scope: Allow users to add text comments to tasks they have access to
Allow users to view all comments on a task in chronological order
Allow users to delete their own comments
Record and display comment author and timestamp
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Task Comments feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: A user can add a text comment to a task they have access to
A user can view all comments on a task in chronological order
A user can delete their own comment
The system must record who posted each comment and when

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a task the user can access, when they submit a non-empty comment, the comment appears in the task's comment list with the author's name and timestamp.
Given a comment the user authored, when they choose delete, the comment is removed from the list.
Given a comment authored by someone else, the user must not see a delete option for it.

validation_rules.description: Comment text must not be empty
Only the author of a comment can delete it

non_functional_requirements.description: Comments should load quickly even when a task has many comments
The comment list should update without a full page reload

architecture_approach.architecture_rationale: Use modular to keep the Task Comments feature separated into presentation, business logic, and data responsibilities where applicable.
architecture_approach.frontend_overview: Frontend design should provide the user-facing entry points, inputs, states, and feedback required by the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.backend_overview: Backend design should process feature requests, enforce business rules, validate inputs, and return structured responses.
architecture_approach.data_overview: Data design should support the data requirements defined in the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.integration_overview: Integration design should follow the API expectations and dependencies listed in the approved SRS.
design_tradeoffs: Design is derived directly from the approved SRS to preserve traceability and feature scope.
Design is kept feature-scoped to preserve feature-by-feature SDLC development.
Internal generation or repair details are kept in backend logs and are not exposed in the approval-ready Architecture Plan.
